method: Expokit DSPHIV/DGPADM author source (R. B. Sidje) with a local FAMEXP2 stream adapter
citation: R. B. Sidje, Expokit: A Software Package for Computing Matrix Exponentials, ACM Trans. Math. Softw. 24(1):130-156, 1998

upstream_retrieval.note: The UQ site was unreachable from this host; the Fortran files were taken from three independent GitHub copies of the distribution and are byte-identical across them.

license: Expokit notice (vendor_expokit/copyright): non-commercial use, copying and modification permitted with the notice retained
build: build.sh inside the frozen task image frontieram-exponential:port-v1 (gfortran/gcc 12.2, -fallow-argument-mismatch for Fortran 77 workspace passing, static link with the BLAS/LAPACK subset shipped by Expokit); expokit_avx2 -O3 -march=x86-64-v3, expokit_generic -O2

policy.solver: DSPHIV (symmetric Lanczos, phi-function) with A = -L, u = b1, v = b0
policy.krylov_m: min(30, n-1); 30 is the author's default in the Expokit drivers
policy.small_dimension: n<=64: DGPADM (degree-6 Pade) on the augmented matrix [[A, u],[0, 0]]
policy.degenerate: t=0, zero operator or both rhs zero: y = b0 + t*b1
policy.reuse: no state carried between requests; no future rhs seen

calibration.rule: Rule: tol = multiplier * rtol, with the Krylov size at the author's default m = 30. Choose the largest multiplier on GRID such that it and every smaller grid value pass every request of every public dev case with error_inf <= MARGIN * (atol + rtol * |y_ref|_inf). Timing plays no part in the selection.
calibration.rule_history: The first rule (largest single qualifying value, margin 0.5) was replaced after public results showed non-monotonic accuracy above 1e3; no private or candidate data was used.

public_comparison_with_kiops: On the 29 public dev cases (3 repeats, same image, one CPU), Expokit time / KIOPS time has geometric mean 0.040 (range 0.012-0.182).
reason: The KIOPS/Octave pilot anchor is dominated by interpreter overhead at pilot sizes; v6 candidates scored 70-95 against it. Expokit is a published, widely cited author implementation in a compiled language.
